correctness.rationale: Hölder duality gives the full width 2||u||_q. Strict norm comparison localizes the tails to the 2d signed axes or 2^d signed diagonals. In the orthogonal tangent chart, area density tends to one. The leading axis contact is (2/q)sum|z_i|^q for q<2 and a deficit ||z||² for q>2; differentiating the q-norm on the sphere at a diagonal gives Hessian (q-2)f_q I for the half-width and the claimed full-width quadratic coefficient. Uniform radial sandwiches yield the four volumes and their conditional uniform-ball limits. Taylor expansion on the closed simplex is uniform since x^a log^k x stays bounded near a=1, yielding (W-2)/(2-q)=H/2+O_d(|q-2|). Squared Gaussian coordinates give the Dirichlet law. At an axis the entropy is r²log(1/r²)+O_d(r²) uniformly in angle, so H≤2t has squared radius asymptotic to 2t/log(1/t); at a diagonal H=log d-2||z||²+O_d(||z||³). This verifies both entropy constants and marks with the correct extremizer multiplicities and full-width normalization.
residual_risks: The angular replay corroborates finite examples only; the uniform local expansions supply the limit and marked statements. The proof is fixed dimension and gives no joint crossover formula as deficit and q-2 vanish together.

evidence: The inspected passages treat geometric moments/sections/mean width, bounds for expected spherical q-norms, and sharp high-dimensional deviations, respectively.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A moment estimate or a large-d asymptotic with its own scaling does not supply a fixed-d small-deficit equivalent. Standard local volume arguments suffice to derive the theorem after the relevant contacts have been found; those general methods are not themselves novel.

evidence: Projection duality fixes the same observable but gives no shrinking neighborhoods or contact coefficients. The chord theorem samples different directions/offsets and uses chord deficits. Spherical moment results do not distinguish a nonsmooth axis minimum from a quadratic diagonal cap or supply the lower Shannon logarithm.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the existing geometric identification; it does not mechanically imply the precise fixed-d constants, the change of scaling in the Shannon limit, or the corresponding conditional tangent laws.

evidence: For T_i=U_i² and alpha=q/2, log(W/2)=(1-alpha)H_alpha(T)/(2alpha); consequently an equivalent Dirichlet Rényi endpoint theorem at the same parameters would cover these width constants. Kaufmann explicitly identifies the random direction projection length with twice a conjugate norm. The strongest distinct catalogue hit takes random lines and Euclidean chord length, not Haar directional support width. The broad web lookup produced no usable comparison and is not negative evidence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These equivalences credit the standard model and set the proper target for a prior implication. Conditioning a random affine line to intersect a body yields a different distribution and endpoint geometry; the chord law cannot be transferred by mere renaming.

The support-function identity, spherical norm model, Rényi reparametrization, and Gaussian/Dirichlet sampling identity are standard and are not credited as new.

value.rationale: The tails quantify how frequently random directions see nearly extremal full widths and how those directions are distributed within their shrinking neighborhoods. The singular axis law versus quadratic contacts is a genuine difference, and the logarithmic Shannon endpoint explains why the near-Euclidean behavior is not read off by holding q fixed. Precise constants and changes of local shape are useful even in fixed finite dimension.
residual_risks: No joint dimension limit, true joint Euclidean-deficit crossover, or result for random chords is claimed.
